messages.author: 598eae3a5857142f
messages.subject: Bug in placement of ticks
parts:
Hi,

personally I would say the ticks are too low/too far to the left.

code:
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_bw(10))

data <- read.csv("data.csv")
p <- ggplot(data,aes(x=P,y=R,colour=Section,label=Section))
p = p + geom_text(size=5)

p = p + scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(58,88,10),limits=c(58,88),
expand=c(0,0))
p = p + scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(86,95,3), limits=c(86,95.15),
expand=c(0,0))

ggsave(file="~/foo.pdf",width=4.3,height=4.0)

data:
Section,P,R
A, 94.10,78.31
B, 90.19,75.73
C, 94.73,85.46
D, 90.62,74.78
E, 86.47,58.81
F, 92.88,68.48
G, 94.70,80.06
H, 93.60,87.49

result:
http://bit.ly/r1xDL3

best,
Thomas

I see what you are seeing, but I don't think it is a bug. The grey
lines are not axis lines, but panel borders. The panel borders are such
that the outer edge of them are at the specified locations (58 and 86,
in your example). Tick lines are centered on their position. So the
two don't line up. It is more dramatic and obvious with:

p + opts(panel.border = theme_rect(size = 10, colour = "red"))

The outer edge of the red rectangle lines up with the center of the tick
mark.

> Thomas
